name: scalar product 1
questiontext:
The scalar product of two vectors in \(R^3\) is given by

\[{{CT:0}} \cdot {{CT:1}} = {{CT:2}}\]

Let us review the basic properties of scalar properties: 

  1. Linearity: \( (av+bu) \cdot w = a v \cdot w + b u \cdot w, \quad \forall a,b \in R, u,v,w \in R^3 \)
  2. Symmetry: \( v \cdot w = w \cdot v, \quad \forall v,w \in R^3\)
  3. Positivity: \(v \cdot v \ge 0 \) with equality holding if and only if \(v = 0\) is the zero vector. 

The scalar product immediately enables us to calculate a few geometric properties: 

  • Length of a vector: \(||v|| = \sqrt{v \cdot v}\). This is also reffered to as the norm of the vector \(v\). The positivity axiom assures that the number within the square root is always non-negative. 
  • The angle \(\phi\) between two vectors \(v,w \in R^n\) is given by: \( \cos(\phi) = \frac{v \cdot w}{||v|| ||w||}\). The fact that the number on the right of the equation is in \([-1,1]\) and therefore is indeed a cosine of an angle is known as the Cauchy-Schwartz inequality.
  • The projection of the vector \(w\) on the linear subspace \(Span(v)\) is given by: \[Pr_{span(v)}(w) = \frac{w \cdot v}{v \cdot v} v\]. Note that this projection is a vector, which is a scalar multiple of \(v\). 

Let us make sure we understand how to carry out these calculations with the vectors: 

\(v = {{CT:3}}, w = {{CT:4}}.\)

Calculate:

The inner product \(v \cdot w \) = [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

The norm \(||v||\) = [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]]

The cosine of the angle \(\phi\) between these two vectors \(\cos(\phi)\) = [[input:ans3]][[validation:ans3]]

The projection \(Pr_{span(v)}(w)\) = [[input:ans4]] [[validation:ans4]]

How to enter: each entry in its own box: a number, a fraction (e.g. 1/2) or an expression (e.g. sqrt(2)).

on_false.feedback:
• You made a mistake calculating the scalar product. The correct calculation is:

\[{{CT:3}}.{{CT:4}} = {@a1@} = {{CT:5}}\]

on_true.feedback: • The calculation of the norm \(||v||\) is correct.
• It appears that you forgot the square root in the calculation \(||v||=\sqrt{v\cdot v}\).

on_false.feedback:
• You made a mistake calculating the norm. The correct calculation is:

\[\left|\left| {{CT:3}} \right|\right| = {@a2@} = {{CT:6}}\]
• Your calculation for \(cos(\phi)\) is wrong. Remember the formula is \( \cos(\phi) = \frac{v \cdot w}{||v|| ||w||}\).

on_true.feedback: • Your calculation for the projection is correct.

on_false.feedback:
• Something is wrong with the way you calculated the projection. Recall the formula: 

\[Pr_{span(v)}(w) = \frac{w \cdot v}{v \cdot v} v\]

In our case:

\[ \frac{w \cdot v}{v \cdot v} = {@scal@}, v = {{CT:3}}\]

Multiplying the vector by the scalar (each entry separately) yields:

\[Pr_{span(v)}(w) = \frac{w \cdot v}{v \cdot v} v = {{CT:7}}\]
